title: xAI's Turbine Trouble: More Noise, More Power, More Lawsuits
caption:
xAI is facing a lawsuit over the "constant, droning noise" from its gas turbines in Austin. Their response? File to add *more* turbines, effectively doubling the facility's capacity. This isn't just a local dispute; it's a stark preview of AI's escalating energy demands and the environmental trade-offs.

slides.sub: Elon Musk's xAI faces a lawsuit for its data center noise, then doubles down on gas power.

slides.title: The Turbine Tangle
slides.body: Residents near xAI's Austin data center sued over "constant, droning noise" from its gas turbines. These aren't just for backup; they're primary power sources for the AI compute.

slides.title: Why So Many Turbines?
bullets: Training large language models like Grok demands colossal electricity.
Traditional grid infrastructure often can't deliver enough power rapidly.
On-site gas turbines offer a quick, albeit noisy and polluting, solution.
slides.footer: This is a glimpse into AI's growing energy crisis.

audiences.body: Enduring constant industrial noise and air pollution from the turbines, impacting quality of life and property values.
Concerned about increased carbon emissions and reliance on fossil fuels in an era demanding clean energy transition.
Facing scrutiny for their environmental footprint and the escalating cost/complexity of powering advanced models.
